info.name: Agentic SDLC - Verify Steps 1-5
info.description: Exercise the orchestrator workflow, governance, lineage, replanning, and metrics. Requests that depend on async completion are sent manually after checking the preceding status.

exec: pm.test('health endpoint responds OK', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Creates the main run and saves its runId to the collection.
Send after the run reaches DESIGN. Expected status is WAITING_APPROVAL and DESIGN is AWAITING_APPROVAL.

exec: pm.test('run is waiting for design approval', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('WAITING_APPROVAL'); pm.expect(body.nodes.DESIGN).to.eql('AWAITING_APPROVAL'); });

request.description: Approving publishes the held design artifacts and resumes the run.
Wait briefly after approval, then send until status is SUCCEEDED. Both fork branches and the join must succeed.

exec: pm.test('all five graph nodes succeeded', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('SUCCEEDED'); ['REQUIREMENTS','DESIGN','IMPLEMENT','TEST_PLAN','RELEASE_READINESS'].forEach(function (id) { pm.expect(body.nodes[id], id + ' state').to.eql('SUCCEEDED'); }); });

request.description: Checks that RELEASE_READINESS started after both parallel branches succeeded.

exec: pm.test('join waited for both branches', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const events = pm.response.json(); const done = events.filter(e => e.eventType === 'STATE_TRANSITION' && e.toState === 'SUCCEEDED' && ['IMPLEMENT','TEST_PLAN'].includes(e.nodeId)); const join = events.find(e => e.eventType === 'STATE_TRANSITION' && e.nodeId === 'RELEASE_READINESS' && e.toState === 'RUNNING'); pm.expect(done.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(join).to.exist; pm.expect(Date.parse(join.occurredAt)).to.be.at.least(Math.max.apply(null, done.map(e => Date.parse(e.occurredAt)))); });

request.description: Inspect active versions and lineageJson input artifact IDs, versions, and hashes.

exec: pm.test('artifacts include lineage', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const artifacts = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(artifacts.length).to.be.greaterThan(0); const changeset = artifacts.find(a => a.type === 'CODE_CHANGESET' && a.active); pm.expect(changeset).to.exist; pm.expect(changeset.lineageJson).to.include('API_SPEC'); });

request.description: After the primary run succeeds, re-executes IMPLEMENT and its downstream RELEASE_READINESS join.
Resend until SUCCEEDED; inspect timeline/artifacts to see new versions.

exec: pm.test('replanned run succeeded', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('SUCCEEDED'); pm.expect(body.nodes.IMPLEMENT).to.eql('SUCCEEDED'); pm.expect(body.nodes.RELEASE_READINESS).to.eql('SUCCEEDED'); });

request.description: Marks IMPLEMENT rolled back, restores earlier active artifact versions when available, and invalidates downstream results.
Restores a complete successful run after the rollback verification.

exec: pm.test('replan after rollback accepted', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(202); });

request.description: Uses a deliberately fake credential string to verify the no-secrets policy blocks generated artifacts.

exec: pm.test('policy check run accepted', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(202); });

request.description: Send after the policy run finishes. Expect a POLICY_CHECK no-secrets BLOCK and a failed/blocked run, with no secret value in the audit reason.

exec: pm.test('policy denial is audited without echoing the value', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const body = pm.response.json(); const policy = body.find(e => e.eventType === 'GATE_EVALUATED' && e.reason.includes('POLICY_CHECK:no-secrets')); pm.expect(policy).to.exist; pm.expect(policy.reason).to.include('BLOCK'); pm.expect(policy.reason).not.to.include('example-only-credential'); });

request.description: Creates a second run for the safe-stop check. Save its runId and wait until it reaches the DESIGN approval checkpoint before stopping it.
Send once the run status is WAITING_APPROVAL. Expected response is 202; run status then becomes SAFE_STOPPED.
Creates a third run to verify rejection followed by an explicit retry.
Wait for DESIGN to reach AWAITING_APPROVAL before sending.
Retries DESIGN; because its approval gate still applies, the run should pause for approval again.
Send after the retried DESIGN reaches AWAITING_APPROVAL.
Run after the primary, policy, safe-stop, and retry checks. Inspect counters and durations for each workflow action.

exec: pm.test('metrics endpoint responds and includes workflow meters', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const body = pm.response.text(); pm.expect(body).to.include('orchestrator_runs_started_total'); pm.expect(body).to.include('orchestrator_gates_evaluated_total'); pm.expect(body).to.include('orchestrator_node_attempts_total'); pm.expect(body).to.include('orchestrator_run_duration_seconds'); pm.expect(body).to.include('orchestrator_retries_total'); pm.expect(body).to.include('orchestrator_rollbacks_total'); pm.expect(body).to.include('orchestrator_safe_stops_total'); });
